title: Childhood home and neighbor Buddy Bolin
summary: He was born at 2319 First Street, moved to Third and Clara around age five or six, and later to Broadmoor. Harry relays what his brothers and half sister told him about Buddy Bolin, a fine cornetist who was confined as mentally ill and later played trombone; Russell gives his dates.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, what part of town were you raised in and where were you... What part of town were you born in and all?
Uh, well I was born on First Street, First and Liberty. 2319 First Street.
When we were... When I was about five or six years old, we moved to Third, Third and Clara. And we lived there up until about 1928. And we moved right back in Broadmoor, where I'm living now. Yes.

Of course... When I talked to you about, oh, it's been, I guess, 10 years ago, once at the famous door, I think you told me you remembered when you were a boy hearing music up in the neighborhood, some of the colored... Was it Buddy Bolin or somebody near there?
Well, there were a lot of colored people around there. Well, Buddy Bolin, I really didn't know him. He, I think he died before my time, but my older brothers knew him.
Yep. I think he...

Jimmy, he just died about a little over a year ago. He was, I think, 71, 72, maybe a little over a year. When he died. He was in his seventies, yeah. Well, he knew Buddy Bolin. Uh-huh. And Buddy lived two doors from us, so he told me.
Uh-huh.

And, uh, I have an older sister. She's still living. She's the only relative I have now. She's a half-sister. Yeah. She's in her eighties. And she knew Buddy Bolin and his sister and mother when she was young. Well, they're spoken about Buddy. My brother, especially, he's spoken about him quite a bit.
Jim?
Jim, yeah. He said he was a real fine cornet player and he took sick, mentally ill, and he was confined. And then he came out and when he came out, my brother said he played fine trombone.
Played trombone then later?
Played fine trombone. He said he practiced the trombone while he was confined.
Uh-huh.
And he came out and played trombone. He said he played very good. Uh-huh. But, uh, then he went back and I understand he died there.
Yes, I think he died in 1931. Uh-huh. I think he was committed to the asylum in 1907, I believe is the date.
Uh-huh.
So you would have only been seven or eight years old when that happened. Yeah.
Yeah.
I don't remember for sure. That's one advantage in having the tape recording. We can remember what people say from now on. Uh-huh. When I first talked to you, I think he said that.
Jimmy never mentioned when he was committed.
